llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions largely match its stated purpose (automating an external platform) but there are several practical security and hygiene issues (hardcoded weak password, plaintext credential storage, missing dependency checks, and unknown upstream trust) that make me wary.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (automate AI Credit Share platform actions) aligns with included scripts and SKILL.md. The skill uses HTTP calls to the aicreditshare.com API and stores agent credentials locally; these are consistent with the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs network API use and examples match the scripts. However the shipped init.sh and aics.sh will register/login and read/write ~/.aicreditshare/config.json (storing API keys/secrets/tokens in plaintext) and init.sh uses a hardcoded password 'Test123456' for registration — behavior not explicit in SKILL.md and potentially unsafe. The scripts also assume openssl is available (used to compute HMAC) but init.sh only checks curl/jq.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads; the skill is instruction + local scripts included in the package. Nothing is fetched or executed from arbitrary URLs during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables and does not ask for unrelated credentials. It does persist API keys/secrets/tokens into ~/.aicreditshare/config.json in plaintext, which is disproportionate from a security perspective (sensitive secrets written to disk without encryption).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no modifications to other skills or global agent settings. The skill writes its own config under the user's home directory (~/.aicreditshare) which is normal for a client tool, but this persistent credential storage increases risk if credentials are sensitive.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package looks coherent for automating the named platform, but exercise caution before installing or running it.

Key points to consider:
- The init script auto-registers/logs in and writes API credentials and tokens in plaintext to ~/.aicreditshare/config.json. If those credentials grant financial or sensitive access, storing them unencrypted is risky.
- The registration call uses a hardcoded weak password (Test123456). Either change the password immediately after registration or avoid automatic registration and create accounts manually.
- The aics.sh script computes HMAC signatures using the openssl CLI but the installer only checks for curl and jq; ensure openssl is present and inspect the HMAC usage if you care about signature secrecy.
- The remote API domain (https://www.aicreditshare.com) is the only external endpoint used—verify you trust that domain and, if possible, review the upstream repository or official docs before using.
- Prefer running the init/CLI scripts in an isolated environment (throwaway VM or container) on first run to observe behavior. Manually inspect ~/.aicreditshare/config.json, and consider encrypting or removing stored credentials when not needed.

If you need higher assurance, request the upstream repository or a signed release, and verify that the API endpoints and auth model match your security requirements.
